subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw replace native extra-bootstrap glob collection and bootstrap-hook scheduling with this cooperative implementation while accepting ownership of its compatibility and session-context semantics?
rationale: The patch is technically sound and well-proven, but green tests cannot decide whether the runtime should permanently own native-glob parity or whether the scheduling change is acceptable for existing hook implementations.

options.title: Accept after exact-head checks
options.body: Approve the compatibility boundary, refresh exact-head CI and the three-way merge review, then land the current focused implementation.

options.title: Require live channel proof
options.body: Request one loaded Gateway run showing channel keepalives and message delivery remain responsive during a large bootstrap scan before accepting the runtime change.

options.title: Pause for a narrower design
options.body: Hold the PR while an owner chooses a smaller native-glob or worker-isolation approach, accepting that the reported current-main stall remains unresolved.

recommendation.title: Accept after exact-head checks
recommendation.body: Approve the compatibility boundary, refresh exact-head CI and the three-way merge review, then land the current focused implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to both bootstrap-context behavior and internal-hook runtime decisions.
